shipped_fit.specification: within (event, lap) transform of lap time and of every fixed-effect column (exact_within); compound offset + compound x tyre-age slope + traffic; random circuit slope, driver-in-event intercept, run intercept, run slope; REML

engine_agreement.specification: circuit random slope + driver-in-event + run intercept

warnings: Maximum Likelihood optimization failed to converge. Check mle_retvals
MixedLM optimization failed, trying a different optimizer may help.
The Hessian matrix at the estimated parameter values is not positive definite.
The MLE may be on the boundary of the parameter space.

old_fit_reproduction.note: Same model, same data. The unscaled L-BFGS fit stops early with a flagged non-converged, non-positive-definite result; the rescaled fit converges to a circuit-slope SD far smaller.

inference_comparison.reading: Widths relative to the lap-level circuit model (B). Run-level terms and cluster-robust errors answer 'how many independent observations are there'.

circuit_effect.model: random circuit slope + driver-in-event + run intercept + run slope; REML; null = same without the circuit slope

lr_test.p_floor_note: with B replicates the smallest attainable p is 1/(B+1)

shrunken_predictions_not_an_effect_size.why: predicted random effects are shrunk toward zero; their range neither estimates nor bounds the true circuit SD

per_race_separation.caveat: The benchmark width is one driver's three stints at one race; ours is a whole field's stints at one race. Width is not like for like, and the benchmark's own tightening is partly just more data. The adjacent-pair counts are within-event and so are free of the compound-circuit confound.

simulation_based_calibration.what_it_tests: the estimator against data drawn from the fitted model itself; it cannot detect misspecification

lap_level_calibration.what: held-out LAPS inside their predictive interval, leave-one-run-out; dominated by lap scatter, says little about the rates

ablation.practitioner_definition: fuel-corrected lap time on tyre age, within driver x stint (fixed effects), per physical compound, run-clustered SE; track evolution and traffic NOT controlled

power.design_notes: 13 circuits, 20-lap stints, 3 stints per driver-event, two compounds; balanced = both at every circuit, split = disjoint circuits

original_welch_calculation.what_it_ignores: circuit variance, stint-level wear variation, run correlation

design.compounds: physical C numbers (2022-25 from Pirelli nomination history, 2026 from allocation.json)

exact_vs_approximate.what: Same laps, same random effects, same REML engine; only the construction of the fixed-effect columns differs. exact: tilde(D_c) offsets (one reference compound) and tilde(D_c x raw tyre age) slopes; approximate: raw D_c offsets and D_c x tilde(age) slopes.

event_cluster_bootstrap.note: Races redrawn with replacement; a repeated race counts as two blocks. Resamples missing a compound (C1 runs at only two races) are dropped and counted.

compound_spread_2026.note: In 2026 each circuit hosts one race, so this circuit SD is race-to-race variance.

power_extended.design_notes: 13 events with the actual 2026 Pirelli nominations; 20-lap stints; N counts stints of the two compared compounds; balanced = both at every circuit; split = disjoint circuits

min_detectable_effect.note: mde_80 = smallest compound gap (s/lap) with 80% power; analytic uses known variances (a lower bound on the detectable gap), simulated refits them. 'crossing' keys are effects, not stints.

detectable_from_fit.what: Smallest true gap in wear rate between neighbouring compounds that the REAL data would detect with 80% power (two-sided 5% Wald test), from each fit's own covariance; not a simulation and not the idealised design of power_extended.
detectable_from_fit.units: seconds per lap of tyre age; contrast 'Cb-Ca' is rate(Cb) minus rate(Ca)

shipped_2026.specification: shipped race fit: compound offsets and tyre-age slopes, traffic, random circuit slope, driver-in-event, run intercept, run slope; REML

pooled_2022_26_nested.specification: circuit random slope plus race-within-circuit random slope, C-number compounds, run terms as shipped; REML

detectable_from_fit.caveats: Wald z with fitted variance components treated as known; the t-reference column shows how much larger the detectable gap is when the number of independent races or circuits is small.

mundlak_check.question: Is a run's random pace level unrelated to its tyre age? (Mundlak / correlated random effects)
mundlak_check.device: fixed covariates = run mean of the model's own tyre-age regressor for that run's compound (tilde(D_c x raw age) / SD, exactly within-transformed), one per compound; slopes then use within-run variation only

wald_run_means_zero.note: Wald chi-square from the CRE fit's own covariance, variance components treated as known.

bootstrap_t.reading: Share of cluster-bootstrap replicates whose statistic for (delta* - delta_hat) reaches the observed one; calibrates the chi-square to the small number of independent races.

hausman.variance_of_difference: V(CRE) - V(RE) on the compound slopes (RE efficient under H0)

cluster_by_event.note: lo/hi and p use t with G-1 df; lo_conservative/hi_conservative use t with (clusters carrying the compound - 1) df, the honest reading for a compound that few clusters carry

bootstrap.note: races redrawn with replacement (one drawn twice counts as two blocks), RE and CRE refitted on each resample; replicates where either fit did not converge are dropped; a compound absent from a resample is left out of that compound's statistics.

wald_run_means_zero.note: Wald chi-square from the CRE fit's own covariance, variance components treated as known.

bootstrap_t.reading: Share of cluster-bootstrap replicates whose statistic for (delta* - delta_hat) reaches the observed one; calibrates the chi-square to the small number of independent races.

hausman.variance_of_difference: V(CRE) - V(RE) on the compound slopes (RE efficient under H0)

cluster_by_event.note: lo/hi and p use t with G-1 df; lo_conservative/hi_conservative use t with (clusters carrying the compound - 1) df, the honest reading for a compound that few clusters carry

cluster_by_circuit.note: lo/hi and p use t with G-1 df; lo_conservative/hi_conservative use t with (clusters carrying the compound - 1) df, the honest reading for a compound that few clusters carry

bootstrap.note: circuits redrawn with replacement (one drawn twice counts as two blocks), RE and CRE refitted on each resample; replicates where either fit did not converge are dropped; a compound absent from a resample is left out of that compound's statistics.

regulation_sensitivity.question: Is pooling 2026 (new rules, narrower tyres) with 2022-2025 (one rule set) driving the pooled results?
